recipes.name: Baked Halibut Sitka
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds halibut fillet, cut into 6 pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C).
Season halibut with salt and ground black pepper.
Place halibut in the greased baking dish.
Combine green onions, mayonnaise, sour cream, and dill in a bowl.
Spread green onion mixture evenly over each halibut piece.
Bake in the preheated oven until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork, about 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Halibut Sitka
raw_recipe.description: Halibut fillets baked in a creamy sauce with dill and green onions make a perfect dish for dinner parties or any night of the week.

review.reviewBody: Really, really good! I made the recipe to a T - didn't change a thing and everyone loved it. Some paprika or seafood seasoning on the fish itself might be a nice touch. Next time, and there will be a next time!

This was very tasty...bf said I could make this again anytime:)
I followed the idea of another reviewer and put melted butter, about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh squeezed lemon juice and same amount of white wine in the pan followed by the halibut, covered with the mayo/sour cream/green onion/dill mixture, then sprinkled it with fresh bread crumbs and lastly sprinkled it lightly with shredded cheddar cheese. I baked it at 400 degrees F for 25 minutes (the fish was still pretty chilled inside) instead of the 475 degree temp in the recipe and it came out perfect! 130 degrees internal temp. Thank you jalexandropoulos for the recipe!!

Amazing simple reciepe! Nothing was left at my dinner party, but it's halibut so not surprised. Spouse gave this version with my modifications a 16/10. Unheard of in this house hold. So These are some of the changes I made. My child is anaphylactic to eggs so mayo is not an option, so made the cream sauce with only the sour cream but used a full cup to compensate for my no mayo use. I also didn't have green onions on hand so I sautéed regular onions in olive oil with minced garlic. I then put them all together (sour cream, onions garlic, dill) in my food processor and whipped it together with (Salt & pepper to taste) I salted pepper and garlic powdered seasoned the fish both sides and put into my compact dish. At the bottom of the dish I squeezed half a lemon, some white wine and melted butter, and poured it into the bottom of the dish and then layer my fish on top, poured/spread my cream base over all the fish, then I took my Italian style bread crumbs to make a crust and added a light layer of cheddar cheese. Baked it for the allotted time then switched my oven to broil @555 to make the topping crispy. Mmmmmmmmm! Delish!
This was very tasty, I added 2 Tbl spoons of grated parmesan and a squeeze of lemon juice. Cooked at 400* for 18 min than broiled for the last 2 min.

Great recipe!
I try following recipes exactly the first time I make them, but didn't have green onions so used chopped white onion instead. It still turned out delicious, and I'm sure with green onion it would be even better.

I baked the filet (approx. 1" thick) at 400 for 15 minutes.
I agree with the other reviewer that 20 minutes at 475 degrees would definitely result in overcooked fish (and I like my fish well done).
Amazing flavor! I’ve made it with halibut and cod. Both were delicious! One time I sprinkled panko bread crumbs on top before baking. It was great!

Love this! I have alot of fish from Alaska and am always looking for new recipes. This was SO easy and SO good!!! I wouldn't make as much sauce next time. Maybe 1/3 cup each because it was alot of sauce even for a big piece of fish. I tried to reduce heat to 400 for 12 minutes but my piece of fish was to big. That would be perfect for smaller pieces of fish as the small part of mince was done. After I turned it up to 425 for 10 more minutes and it was perfect! Sprinke a little paprika on at the end...and YUM!!!!! Can't wait to make this again!

I had some halibut stashed in the freezer and decided to give this a try. It was very good! I baked this in individual oval Corningware dishes, which helped to contain the yummy sauce. I didn’t think an oven temperature as high as 475 was necessary, so I baked mine at 400 degrees and they were perfectly cooked in 20-25 minutes. I think 20 minutes at 475 would have overcooked the fish. This is super easy and we enjoyed it.

1-12-2016 ~I'm lucky to have beautiful halibut filets in the freezer we hauled back from a trip to Seattle. Hubs has always said he dislikes it, preferring firmer fish like salmon or swordfish, but I just can't eat it all myself while he grills himself a steak. I took a chance making this tonight and much to my pleasure and surprise, we BOTH liked it. I didn't have green onions at hand but frozen chives filled in nicely. I wasn't confident with the high cooking temperature and 20 minutes at 425 degrees for the thick filets I had worked out fine and perhaps could have used a minute or two less. This doesn't get any easier to make and is surprisingly delicious given how quick it is to throw together and pop in the oven. Give the bonus of Hubs enjoying it too, this is something I won't hesitate to make again - in fact, I'll be eager to. One suggestion however - it needs a little pop of color so give it a little sprinkle of paprika either before or after baking. A spring of parsley or something green upon serving doesn't hurt either.

Everyone is right. This is a fabulous recipe. I used a pound of wahoo rather than halibut. I usd fresh dill instead of dried. I also reduced oven temp to 400 as other suggested. It was perfect after 20 minutes. I added white wine, a little butter and lemon in the bottom before placing the fish. Added a little bread crumbs to the top. I served it with mashed potatoes and green beans with almonds, cranberries and lemon. I will definitely do again but would want it a little lighter, I’d reduce some of the dill/mayo/sour cream sauce that I put on the fish and maybe serve with brown rice or quinoa rather than mashed potatoes.

Wow!! This was really tasty! I did substitute Greek yogurt for sour cream. I used lemon pepper for plain pepper. Roasted veggies in same pan as I made half the portion and had room. Great dinner for two! Thank you for a flavorful fish! Can't wait to make again!
This took 30 minutes at 400. Letting it sit and rest for 5-10 minutes after baking makes a big difference.
I have made with both Halibut and cod fish, I also mixed in graded cheddar and gouda and onions with Xtra sauce. Can eat the sauce on its own.
I added seafood seasoning, garlic powder, and substituted onion powder for the green onions. It was excellent!!
Amazing recipe!!! However, I like 2-3x times the sauce mix because it is INCREDIBLY tasty! So, double or triple it, you will not be sorry! One of my top favorite recipes!
My family loved this dish. It is a definite repeat meal for us
Simple, tasty, easy to make and the family loves it.
